title: SQL injection login bypass with quote filtering
content: For SQL injection tasks, identify the exact parameter and context before choosing a payload pattern. When single quotes are filtered, test numeric-context boolean differences, comment syntax variations, or tool-assisted SQLi validation instead of repeating the same quoted payload. Keep requests scoped to the confirmed endpoint and preserve method/body format from reconnaissance.
applicability: Use when a login or data lookup parameter shows SQL behavior but quotes or comments are filtered.
safety_notes: Controlled pattern guidance only; prefer SmartSQLiTool for automated validation.

security.request_template: POST /login with form body preserving observed field names

title: XSS bypass when script tags are blocked
content: For reflected XSS, first classify the reflection context: HTML text, quoted attribute, unquoted attribute, JavaScript string, URL attribute, JSON, or comment. If script tags are blocked, switch to context-compatible event-handler, tagless, URL-attribute, or JavaScript-string breakout patterns. Preserve the original parameter and validate that the intended trigger string remains intact.
applicability: Use after reconnaissance confirms reflection and filtering of script tags or keywords.
safety_notes: Use only in authorized test targets; avoid unrelated endpoints.

title: Jinja2 SSTI payload placement conventions
content: For Jinja2 SSTI, payload placement matters more than payload memorization. Confirm that user-controlled input reaches a template expression context, then place the test value in the observed query parameter, form field, header, or JSON key. If curly braces or quotes are filtered, try arithmetic probes, alternate delimiters where supported, or context changes rather than blind repetition.
applicability: Use when Python/Jinja2 template rendering is suspected and a parameter is reflected or evaluated.
safety_notes: Keep probes non-destructive and evidence-driven before exploitation.

title: Twig template injection request template
content: For Twig SSTI, verify the endpoint, method, and input field that reaches template rendering. Use low-impact expression probes first and preserve the request body format exactly. If the field is in a form, keep content-type form-urlencoded; if it is JSON, keep JSON syntax and quote escaping intact.
applicability: Use when PHP/Symfony/Twig is suspected and input is rendered in a template.
safety_notes: Do not jump to command execution before confirming template evaluation.

security.request_template: POST /preview with form body using the observed field name

title: Command injection through shell metacharacter filtering
content: For command injection, infer the shell context and blocked metacharacters from response behavior. If semicolons are filtered, consider newline, ampersand, pipe, command substitution, encoded separators, or tool-specific command injection support only when compatible with the observed sink. For blind command injection, use timing confirmation before output retrieval.
applicability: Use when an HTTP parameter reaches a shell command and one separator family is filtered.
safety_notes: Prefer non-destructive commands and bounded validation.

security.request_template: POST /action with observed parameter carrying a minimal timing probe

title: Header-based payload placement
content: Some frameworks route behavior through headers instead of body parameters. If reconnaissance shows a framework-specific header, middleware, routing expression, or proxy behavior, preserve the exact header name and place the test value there. Do not move payloads between body, query, and headers unless evidence suggests the sink consumes that location.
applicability: Use when framework behavior indicates header-based parsing or routing.
safety_notes: This is placement guidance, not a PoC workflow.

security.request_template: GET /endpoint with the exact observed framework header

title: JSON body injection request-template discipline
content: When the injection surface is a JSON body, preserve JSON syntax, content-type, field names, and escaping. Avoid converting JSON into form-urlencoded parameters. If a prior request succeeded with a particular shape, reuse that body shape and change only the controlled value needed for the test.
applicability: Use when Collector summary reports JSON body fields for an injection endpoint.
safety_notes: Keep task instructions atomic and scoped to the confirmed endpoint.

security.request_template: POST /api with Content-Type: application/json and observed field names
